record.context_brief: genus algorithms with fixed non-orientable genus
record.original_question: For each fixed non-orientable genus k, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that computes the orientable genus of a graph whose non-orientable genus is k?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.1 For each fixed k, there is a polynomial-time algorithm to calculate the orientable genus of a graph with non-orientable genus k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The orientable genus of a graph G, denoted g(G), is the smallest nonnegative integer g such that G admits a cellular embedding in the orientable closed surface of genus g (the sphere with g handles attached). The non-orientable genus of G, denoted \tilde g(G), is the smallest positive integer k such that G admits a cellular embedding in the non-orientable closed surface N_k (the sphere with k crosscaps); by convention, planar graphs are also allowed. Computing either genus is known to be NP-hard in general, but for each fixed surface there is a linear-time algorithm that decides embeddability.

Question: Does there exist, for each fixed positive integer k, an algorithm with running time polynomial in |V(G)|+|E(G)| that, given as input a graph G with \tilde g(G) = k, outputs the orientable genus g(G)?

Equivalently, prove or disprove that the orientable-genus computation problem, restricted to inputs whose non-orientable genus equals a fixed value k, is solvable in polynomial time.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface no result resolving this conjecture. While Mohar's linear-time algorithm decides embeddability in any fixed surface, and recent works give EPTAS for dense graphs and approximation algorithms for general graphs, no polynomial-time exact algorithm restricted to graphs of fixed non-orientable genus k for computing the orientable genus appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Genus of a Graph: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Computing genus is NP-hard; for each fixed surface there is a linear time algorithm (Mohar) but parameters are doubly-exponential in genus.
status_evidence.claim: No exact polynomial algorithm conditional on fixed non-orientable genus is known.

status_evidence.title: Efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme for the genus of dense graphs
status_evidence.snippet: EPTAS for orientable and non-orientable genus on dense graphs; exact computation remains hard in general.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances are approximate, not exact-polynomial for graphs of fixed non-orientable genus.
